package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes configuration files, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Collected sensitive data is exfiltrated to an external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to user credentials and configuration files.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com during setup.py execution.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing outbound requests to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the installation of 'pymafka' for any attempts to access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config. Flag any outbound network connections to app.threatest.com during the installation process. Automated scanning should inspect setup.py for code that reads sensitive files and sends their contents to external domains, specifically app.threatest.com.
